question: At what point does the growing baby officially change from an embryo to a foetus?

options.A: Moment of successful implantation
options.B: Beginning of the ninth week
options.C: Start of the second trimester
options.D: End of the fourteenth week

explanation: That's correct! Week nine marks the start of the foetal period, where rapid growth and fine-tuning take center stage. You're mastering this topic! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h3)

question: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle much thicker than the right ventricle?

options.A: It receives blood directly from the lungs under high pressure.
options.B: It contracts more frequently than the right side of the heart.
options.C: It holds a much larger volume of blood at rest.
options.D: It must pump blood through the entire systemic circulation.

explanation: Think of the left ventricle as the heavyweight champion of the heart. It needs extra muscle because it has to push blood all the way around your entire body! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T5#GNS123_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells in the testes to start producing testosterone?

options.A: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.D: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: Correct! Luteinizing hormone (LH) is released from the brain and travels down to target the Leydig cells, telling them to pump out testosterone. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h2)

question: What word do we use for the strength of the attraction between a drug and its target receptor?

options.A: Efficacy
options.B: Tolerance
options.C: Affinity
options.D: Potency

explanation: Affinity is just like how strongly a magnet is drawn to metal. It describes how tightly a drug wants to bind to its specific cellular receptor! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h2)

question: In which situation would you expect a patient to be placed on a fluid diet?

options.A: During long-term rehabilitation for a chronic leg fracture
options.B: Immediately following abdominal surgery before bowel sounds return
options.C: As a permanent meal plan for an active adolescent
options.D: To treat long-term iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Right after surgery, the gut is sleeping! Fluids are gentle and safe until the bowel wakes back up. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h2)

question: A nurse reviews whether a patient's blood pressure has decreased after giving a prescribed medication. Which step of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Evaluation
options.B: Implementation
options.C: Planning
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Checking the results of an action to see if the patient's goals were met is the definition of evaluation. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h2)

question: When you add up all the percentages in a pie chart, what must they always equal?

options.A: The median value of the data
options.B: A maximum of 360 degrees
options.C: The total number of patients
options.D: Exactly 100 percent

explanation: Great job! Because a pie chart shows a complete whole, all the slices added together must always make 100 percent. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which mineral does the body need to make thyroid hormones?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Potassium

explanation: Spot on! Iodine is the key building block the thyroid gland uses to produce active hormones. Without enough iodine, the thyroid struggles to do its job. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which nursing action helps thin thick respiratory secretions so they are easier for the patient to cough up?

options.A: Lying the patient flat on their back
options.B: Keeping the room air completely dry
options.C: Encouraging adequate daily fluid intake
options.D: Restricting all drinking water after meals

explanation: Drinking enough water keeps body fluids thin, which naturally loosens thick mucus in the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which body structure is hurt when someone suffers a sprain?

options.A: Tendon
options.B: Muscle
options.C: Cartilage
options.D: Ligament

explanation: A sprain happens when a ligament gets stretched too far or tears. Remember: ligaments connect bone to bone at your joints! You've got this. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T9#GNS222_U1_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of providing regular supportive supervision visits to rural community midwives?

options.A: To increase the paperwork burden without providing clinical assistance
options.B: To offer mentorship, solve operational challenges, and reduce professional isolation
options.C: To look for minor errors so the midwife can be publicly punished
options.D: To replace the midwife with an administrative clerk from the city

explanation: Supportive supervision focuses on guidance, problem-solving, and emotional encouragement rather than fault-finding, keeping rural health workers motivated. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h8)

question: What is the main danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their daily seizure medication?

options.A: It leads to complete kidney failure and lifelong dialysis needs
options.B: It causes immediate permanent blindness within a few hours
options.C: It results in rapid hair loss and severe skin pigmentation changes
options.D: It can trigger status epilepticus, a dangerous and prolonged seizure state

explanation: Stopping antiseizure drugs abruptly shocks the brain, causing a rebound effect that can trigger severe, continuous seizures (status epilepticus). Patients must always taper under medical advice! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h8)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the milk ejection reflex during breastfeeding?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Oxytocin causes the tiny muscles around the milk glands to contract, squeezing the milk out into the ducts for the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h5)

question: Why does severe anxiety or pain interfere with a client's ability to understand health instructions?

options.A: It limits the client's mental capacity to focus on new information
options.B: It forces the nurse to use complex medical terminology
options.C: It prevents the nurse from speaking in a normal tone of voice
options.D: It automatically makes the client deaf to any spoken sound

explanation: When a person is in intense pain or highly anxious, their brain is overwhelmed, making it very difficult to process and retain health teachings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: When you gently feel (palpate) a mother's tummy to check her uterus after birth, what is your main goal?

options.A: To confirm that the uterus is firm and contracting
options.B: To check if the bladder is completely empty
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the breasts
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the mother

explanation: A nice, hard, contracted uterus (like a firm mango!) stops bleeding. If it feels soft or boggy, that's a red flag for postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h4)

question: A teenager in a juvenile facility finishes counseling and medical care. What is the most important next step for long-term success?

options.A: Focusing solely on physical fitness and sports activities
options.B: Providing practical vocational training and skill acquisition
options.C: Keeping the teenager isolated from society indefinitely
options.D: Discharging the youth without any follow-up support

explanation: Brilliant! Teaching a skill or trade gives young people a way to earn an honest living, which keeps them away from future trouble. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which type of dietary fiber is best known for adding bulk to stool and keeping things moving smoothly in the gut?

options.A: Simple fiber
options.B: Glycogen fiber
options.C: Soluble fiber
options.D: Insoluble fiber

explanation: Spot on! Insoluble fiber doesn't break down easily, so it adds bulk and helps prevent constipation. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h5)

question: Which preparation is specifically designed as a liquid instillation into the rectum?

options.A: Transdermal patch
options.B: Enema
options.C: Sublingual tablet
options.D: Suppository

explanation: An enema is a liquid solution instilled into the rectum to either clean the bowel or deliver localized treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h3)

question: Which major health issue deeply affects young people worldwide?

options.A: Unplanned pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Advanced age-related joint degeneration
options.C: Chronic occupational lung diseases
options.D: Severe childhood developmental delays

explanation: Correct! Adolescents face serious reproductive health challenges, which makes targeted education and friendly services so important. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h2)

question: What is a major reason pregnant women might hide their emotional distress from healthcare providers?

options.A: Routine instructions given during antenatal classes
options.B: Complete lack of physical symptoms during gestation
options.C: The absence of hormonal fluctuations in pregnancy
options.D: Fear of being judged and stigmatized as a bad mother

explanation: So true. Stigma makes many mums keep quiet, which is why a warm, non-judgmental nursing approach is so important! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h7)

question: What is the main job of the Theatre Sterile Supply Unit (TSSU)?

options.A: Disposing of hazardous biological waste from wards
options.B: Manufacturing single-use surgical equipment
options.C: Processing, sterilizing, and distributing medical instruments
options.D: Conducting pre-surgery patient assessments

explanation: You've got this! The TSSU is the heartbeat behind every clean surgery. Its main job is to safely clean, sterilize, and hand out surgical tools so patients stay infection-free. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: A patient having a blood transfusion suddenly develops fever, chills, and sharp lower back pain. What is likely happening?

options.A: Delayed iron toxicity
options.B: Circulatory fluid overload
options.C: Simple allergic skin rash
options.D: Acute hemolytic reaction

explanation: Lower back pain, fever, and chills are classic warning signs that the body is reacting against the red blood cells. Great clinical cue to remember! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T11#GNS215_U6_T11_h5)

question: Why is a CT scan with contrast usually preferred for a stable patient with suspected kidney trauma?

options.A: It uses zero radiation and requires no intravenous line placement.
options.B: It can be performed instantly at the bedside without moving an unstable patient.
options.C: It replaces the need to ever inspect the patient's urine for blood.
options.D: It clearly shows active bleeding, urine leaks, and the exact depth of organ damage.

explanation: A contrast CT scan gives doctors a crystal-clear, detailed map showing if blood vessels are bleeding or if urine is leaking into the body. Super helpful tool! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h5)

question: How do remote monitoring devices help a home nurse care for a heart failure patient?

options.A: By replacing the need for physical nursing visits entirely throughout the year
options.B: By diagnosing new cardiac arrhythmias instantly without physician review
options.C: By automatically administering emergency intravenous cardiac medications without human input
options.D: By transmitting daily weight and vital signs remotely to catch worsening fluid retention early

explanation: Remote gadgets let nurses track daily stats so they can spot danger signs and step in before it turns into a hospital emergency. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which imaging test uses a special dye to check if the Fallopian tubes are open?

options.A: Scrotal Doppler ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Hysterosalpingography
options.D: Transvaginal ultrasound

explanation: Brilliant! Hysterosalpingography involves putting dye into the uterus and taking X-rays to see if the fluid flows nicely through open Fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which lethal heart rhythm requires immediate defibrillation and emergency response?

options.A: First-degree heart block
options.B: Sinus bradycardia
options.C: Premature atrial contractions
options.D: Ventricular fibrillation

explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a chaotic heart rhythm where the ventricles quiver instead of pumping blood, causing cardiac arrest that requires immediate electrical shock. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h4)

question: What are the three core functions of public health?

options.A: Inpatient care, pharmacy, and laboratory
options.B: Planning, budgeting, and marketing
options.C: Assessment, policy development, and assurance
options.D: Diagnosis, surgery, and rehabilitation

explanation: The recognized framework for public health activities consists of assessment, policy development, and assurance. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal mortality?

options.A: Benign breast lumps
options.B: Chronic dental caries
options.C: Uncomplicated malaria
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is one of the top direct causes of maternal death worldwide. Knowing how to spot and manage it is essential for every nursing student! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: A patient on hormone therapy for prostate cancer reports hot flashes and fatigue. How should you understand these symptoms?

options.A: Evidence of severe bone marrow suppression caused by the treatment
options.B: Early indicators of metastatic cancer spreading to the brain
options.C: Signs of an acute allergic reaction to the oral medication
options.D: Expected side effects resulting from artificially lowered hormone levels

explanation: Spot on! Lowering hormones mimics natural changes like menopause or andropause, which often brings tiredness and hot flashes. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h4)

question: A patient asks you about the structure of the clitoris. What is a key fact to share with her?

options.A: It disappears completely after a woman goes through puberty.
options.B: It functions mainly to produce mucus for vaginal lubrication.
options.C: It is an internal gland located right next to the cervix.
options.D: Only a small part of it is visible externally, while most extends deep inside.

explanation: You're learning fast! Only the tip (glans) is seen on the outside; the rest of the structure extends deep inside the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T1#GNS121_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is a strict safety rule for a patient being discharged after receiving sedation for an endoscopy?

options.A: They must have a responsible adult escort to take them home.
options.B: They must sign a new consent form before leaving the clinic.
options.C: They must stay in the hospital ward for at least three days.
options.D: They must avoid eating solid food for an entire week.

explanation: Because sedatives stay in the system for hours, patients are not allowed to go home alone or drive themselves. They need a trusted companion! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h8)

question: How do peptide and protein hormones typically travel through the bloodstream?

options.A: They require specialized carrier proteins to move through blood

options.C: They are water-soluble and dissolve freely in blood plasma
options.D: They are fat-soluble and travel inside red blood cells

explanation: Because protein and peptide hormones love water, they dissolve easily right into the watery plasma of your blood and swim along freely without needing a special ride. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h4)

question: How does urine actually travel from the kidneys down to the bladder?

options.A: Cilia beating along the mucosal lining
options.B: Cardiac output and arterial blood pressure
options.C: Passive gravity pulling fluid downward
options.D: Peristaltic smooth muscle contractions

explanation: Fantastic! Even if you are lying flat on your bed, those smooth muscle squeezes keep urine moving nicely. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T2#GNS121_U2_T2_h4)

question: A family's well water is muddy with visible dirt particles. What should they do first before treating it?

options.A: Boil the muddy water without any preparation
options.B: Drink the water quickly before particles dissolve
options.C: Allow the water to undergo sedimentation
options.D: Add large amounts of liquid bleach immediately

explanation: Spot on! Letting the heavy dirt settle to the bottom first (sedimentation) makes cleaning or boiling the water much more effective. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h3)

question: A male patient says he has noticed sexual changes after starting a new heart medication. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Review his medication list to check for known side effects
options.B: Tell him to stop taking all his heart tablets immediately
options.C: Refer him directly for specialized surgical intervention
options.D: Reassure him that all prescription drugs have zero sexual impact

explanation: Correct! Many heart medications are famous for causing sexual side effects. Checking his drug list is a smart and logical first nursing action. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h6)

question: When is the right time to change an absorbent diaper or pad for your patient?

options.A: Right before the doctor arrives for ward round
options.B: As soon as the patient complains of feeling hungry
options.C: Promptly whenever it becomes soiled or wet
options.D: Only once every twenty-four hours during the morning shift

explanation: Don't wait for a schedule if comfort and skin health are on the line. Check frequently and change diapers right away when they are wet or soiled. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h4)

question: What does 'exclusive breastfeeding' mean for a baby during their first six months?

options.A: Combining breast milk with small amounts of clean water
options.B: Receiving breast milk supplemented with medicinal teas
options.C: Receiving only breast milk with no other foods or liquids
options.D: Alternating daily feeds between formula and breast milk

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for patients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: To achieve a complete cure of the genetic mutation
options.B: To stop the natural progression of the disease entirely
options.C: To reverse the physical breakdown of body tissues
options.D: To maximize remaining function and quality of life

explanation: Because these genetic disorders are progressive and incurable, rehabilitation focuses on maintaining independence and quality of life rather than reversing the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h1)

question: If a patient has an injury specifically in the pons, which cranial nerves are most likely to be affected?

options.A: Cranial nerves I and II
options.B: Cranial nerves IX through XII
options.C: Cranial nerves V through VIII
options.D: Cranial nerve III only

explanation: The pons is home to cranial nerves five, six, seven, and eight. So whenever there's trouble in the pons, these are the nerves that usually show it! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h2)

question: What is the most crucial assessment for a nurse to do regularly on a limb with a tumor or post-op reconstruction?

options.A: Checking the patient's visual acuity and pupillary light reflex
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the chest wall every hour
options.C: Neurovascular checks for pulse, color, movement, and sensation
options.D: Auscultating bowel sounds in all four abdominal quadrants

explanation: Swelling or tumor growth can squeeze blood vessels and nerves. Regular checks help us catch circulation issues early and protect the limb! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T19#GNS222_U1_T19_h6)

question: How does political corruption directly hurt maternal and child health programs?

options.A: By building more primary healthcare centers
options.B: By diverting essential medical supplies and funds meant for public clinics
options.C: By lowering the cost of prescription drugs for pregnant women
options.D: By increasing the number of trained midwives in rural villages

explanation: Corruption steals resources meant for the sick, leaving public clinics without basic drugs, working equipment, or safe spaces for mothers. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: A patient who is severely dehydrated is most at risk of experiencing what?

options.A: Immediate thickening of bone tissue matrices
options.B: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells
options.C: Impaired kidney function and electrolyte imbalance
options.D: Excessive accumulation of dense adipose tissue

explanation: When water levels drop too low, blood volume decreases, placing stress on the kidneys and messing up vital body salts (electrolytes). [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h4)

question: What does the top number in a blood pressure reading represent?

options.A: Systolic pressure during heart contraction
options.B: Diastolic pressure during heart relaxation
options.C: Mean arterial pressure across the cardiac cycle
options.D: Central venous pressure inside the right atrium

explanation: The systolic (top) number measures the peak pressure in your arteries when the heart pumps. You're mastering the basics! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: How should a nurse properly clean a medication vial septum before drawing up fluid?

options.A: Blow air heavily onto the rubber top to cool and clean it

options.C: Wipe the top with a dry paper towel immediately before insertion
options.D: Run the entire glass bottle under hot tap water for one minute

explanation: Swabbing the septum with alcohol and letting it dry naturally reduces surface bacteria prior to needle insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: A survivor of forced marriage discloses her situation to a nurse in confidence. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Post the details of the case on social media to raise quick awareness
options.B: Advise the patient to return home and obey her spouse to keep the peace
options.C: Maintain confidentiality while safely connecting her with social services and support
options.D: Inform the village elders immediately to resolve the family dispute

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.A: It only affects internal reproductive organs like the uterus.

options.C: It is performed exclusively in hospital operating theatres.

question: What is your very first priority when a poisoned patient arrives in the emergency unit?

question: Why is a microdrip tubing set (60 gtt/mL) often chosen for infants or sensitive pediatric patients?

options.C: It allows for much smaller, more precise adjustments in fluid delivery.
options.D: It prevents air bubbles from ever entering the patient's bloodstream.

explanation: Microdrip sets produce tiny drops, making it easier to deliver precise fluid volumes and prevent accidental fluid overload in small patients. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which measurement is frequently referred to as the fifth vital sign?

options.A: Weight
options.B: Height
options.C: Urinary output
options.D: Pain

explanation: Pain is routinely assessed alongside traditional vital signs to monitor patient comfort and well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: A patient just had jaw surgery and cannot chew solid foods. Which diet type is best for them?

options.A: High sodium diet
options.B: Standard regular diet
options.C: High residue diet
options.D: Soft or mechanical diet

explanation: Easy choice! Soft and mechanical diets change the texture of food so it's super easy to chew and swallow when the mouth or jaw needs a break. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h3)

question: Which condition is a clear contraindication for performing a joint aspiration?

options.A: An active skin infection directly over the injection site
options.B: Mild swelling in the knee joint after a long walk
options.C: A history of controlled high blood pressure
options.D: Mild stiffness experienced only in the morning

question: Why are worm infections so common in places with poor sanitation?

options.A: Parasitic eggs are easily spread through contaminated soil and water

options.C: Humid air causes human skin to produce worm larvae
options.D: Poor lighting weakens the human immune system against worms

explanation: Spot on! Worm eggs often pass through feces into soil and water supplies, which easily infect new people if hygiene is lacking. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h1)

question: A patient is shaking and sweating, but the meter reads 120 mg/dL. What is your best next step?

options.A: Assume the meter is right and ignore the symptoms
options.B: Repeat the test or consider a lab check
options.C: Leave the patient to rest
options.D: Give rapid-acting insulin

explanation: Always trust your clinical instincts! If the patient's symptoms don't match the number, recheck to be certain. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why do health programs often fail if nurses ignore local cultural values?

options.A: Because government laws forbid treating people with different beliefs
options.B: Because the community feels disrespected and rejects outside interference
options.C: Because local leaders charge heavy fines for unapproved advice
options.D: Because medications lose their chemical potency in different cultures

explanation: Always respect local culture! When people feel understood and respected, they are much more likely to welcome healthcare programs. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h4)

question: In nursing, what does the term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: Using a machine to deliver intravenous fluids
options.B: Taking multiple medications at the same time
options.C: Receiving treatment in a private hospital room
options.D: Having a severe allergy to common antibiotics

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking many drugs at once. This often increases the risk of side effects and drug clashes, so nurses have to monitor these patients closely. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which joint is most likely to suffer first when a patient has a sudden gout attack?

options.A: The hip joint
options.B: The elbow joint
options.C: The shoulder joint
options.D: The big toe

explanation: Great job! The base of the big toe is the classic hotspot for a first-time gout attack. Because of cooler body temperatures there and normal daily pressure, uric acid loves to form crystals in this spot first. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why is tracing sexual partners and notifying them so important after an STI diagnosis?

options.A: It punishes individuals who fail to use proper barrier protection
options.B: It proves whether the patient acquired the infection locally
options.C: It breaks the cycle of reinfection and treats exposed individuals
options.D: It provides statistical data for insurance companies to adjust rates

explanation: Exactly! Partner notification ensures everyone gets tested and treated so they don't keep passing the infection back and forth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)

question: What is a major challenge nurses often face when providing palliative care in resource-limited settings?

options.A: An excess of high-tech equipment that overwhelms patients
options.B: Limited access to essential pain medications and specialized facilities
options.C: A complete absence of family involvement in patient care
options.D: Patients refusing all forms of basic nursing assessment

explanation: In many resource-constrained settings, getting a steady supply of pain relief like opioids can be tough. Nigerian nurses often have to be creative and strong advocates for their patients! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)

question: What is the recommended infant feeding practice for mothers living on ART where replacement feeding is unsafe?

options.A: Exclusive use of herbal teas and plain water
options.B: Immediate weaning onto cow milk on day one
options.C: Strict formula feeding without any breast milk
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months

question: Why is fighting social stigma just as important as medical care in HIV prevention?

options.A: Social attitudes are the only proven cause of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome

options.C: Stigma drives people away from getting tested, seeking counseling, and taking medications
options.D: Overcoming stigma eliminates the need for any safe sex practices

question: Why does the spinal cord have a thicker area called the cervical enlargement?

options.B: To manage sensory and motor input for the upper limbs
options.C: To anchor the spinal cord firmly to the thoracic cage
options.D: To produce extra cerebrospinal fluid for the brain

question: Which of the following is NOT a core ethical principle guiding palliative nursing care?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Punitive dominance
options.D: Non-maleficence

question: A patient with a spinal cord injury is worried about buying daily food and medication after discharge. What should you do first?

options.A: Connect the patient with hospital social welfare services for financial aid options.
options.B: Tell the patient to apply for a bank loan immediately.
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking medication to save money.
options.D: Wait until the patient begs for help before taking any action.

explanation: You're not in this alone! Involving social welfare services helps bridge the gap between a patient's financial stress and available community or government support. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you check when a patient arrives with an acute sting?

options.A: Applying a cold ice pack to reduce swelling
options.B: Assessing airway, breathing, and circulation
options.C: Inquiring about past medical history
options.D: Cleaning the wound with soap and water

explanation: Always ABCs first! Checking airway, breathing, and circulation helps you catch severe allergic reactions or shock before they get out of hand. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: What are the main warning signs of severe pre-eclampsia during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete cessation of fetal movements felt by the mother for two days
options.B: Very high blood pressure accompanied by severe headache and visual changes
options.C: Sudden painless vaginal bleeding in the third trimester of pregnancy
options.D: High fever with generalized body chills and offensive vaginal discharge

explanation: Always watch out for high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches or blurred vision—these are big red flags for pre-eclampsia! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: A patient with advanced dementia makes a pain face, holds their tummy, and has a fast heart rate, but says they have no pain. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient because they cannot feel pain.
options.B: Ignore the physical signs since the verbal denial overrides them.
options.C: Treat these non-verbal behavioral signs as reliable indicators of pain.
options.D: Wait until the patient is able to provide a clear numeric score.

explanation: When dementia makes talking difficult, body language tells the real story. Trust those physical cues! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h5)

question: A fully awake and clear-headed patient says 'No' to a painful procedure. Which ethical principle supports their choice?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Autonomy gives every adult patient the right to self-determination. They own their body, so they get to accept or reject medical treatments based on what matters to them. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why does exclusive breastfeeding often delay the return of normal menstrual periods?

options.A: The placenta continues to secrete high amounts of progesterone postpartum
options.B: High prolactin levels suppress the release of GnRH from the hypothalamus
options.C: Estrogen levels remain permanently depleted while nursing an infant
options.D: The maternal ovaries completely shut down and atrophy after delivery

explanation: Frequent suckling keeps prolactin levels high, which suppresses the release of hypothalamic releasing hormones that stimulate ovulation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h5)

question: Why should nurses care about a patient's social background when talking about reproductive health?

options.A: It ensures the patient will always follow medical advice
options.B: It allows nurses to change national laws regarding healthcare
options.C: It replaces the need for a physical medical examination
options.D: It helps nurses see the real-world barriers affecting patient choices

explanation: You got it! Understanding social factors helps you see the real struggles a patient faces in getting care, making you a more empathetic nurse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h1)

question: A community health nurse organizes a routine childhood vaccination drive at a local clinic. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: You got it! Giving immunizations protects healthy people from getting sick in the first place, which is primary prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h3)

question: You want to build a good relationship with a family caring for an elderly relative at home. What is the best way to start?

options.A: Inform the family of all the household rules they are currently breaking
options.B: Avoid asking personal questions to maintain strict professional distance
options.C: Show sincere interest in the family's daily routines and overall well-being
options.D: Focus exclusively on checking the patient's medication chart immediately

explanation: Showing genuine care for their everyday life helps break the ice and builds a wonderful, trusting relationship beyond just the illness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h3)

question: Why do we call the pancreas a 'heterocrine' (or mixed) organ?

options.A: It releases secretions into both lymphatic vessels and blood capillaries
options.B: Its structure combines neural tissue with glandular epithelial cords
options.C: It produces two opposing hormones, insulin and glucagon, from beta cells
options.D: It contains both exocrine digestive tissue and endocrine hormone-producing islets

explanation: The pancreas wears two hats! It acts as an exocrine gland by sending digestive juices through ducts to your gut, and an endocrine gland by releasing hormones like insulin straight into your blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h5)

question: How do unequal gender roles in a relationship usually affect a woman's reproductive choices?

options.A: She may lack the authority to decide on contraceptive use or family size
options.B: She automatically gains complete control over household finances
options.C: Extended family members lose all interest in her personal life
options.D: Her partner is legally required to consult her on all medical matters

explanation: You got it! In male-dominated settings, women often struggle to make independent choices about birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: Which of these life changes means a female client needs to be refitted for a new diaphragm?

options.A: Changing her brand of body soap
options.B: Starting a daily multi-vitamin
options.C: A minor seasonal head cold
options.D: Significant weight change

explanation: Spot on! Major shifts in weight alter pelvic anatomy, meaning she'll need a new size for a proper, secure seal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h6)

question: Which tiny bumps on the tongue do NOT contain any taste buds?

options.A: Filiform papillae
options.B: Foliate papillae
options.C: Circumvallate papillae
options.D: Fungiform papillae

explanation: Filiform papillae are the most common bumps on your tongue; they give it a rough texture to help move food around, but they do not have taste buds. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T10#GNS211_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of getting a CT scan or MRI for a neurological patient?

options.A: Measuring electrical wave patterns during sleep cycles
options.B: Providing detailed structural images of the brain tissue
options.C: Checking cranial nerve function in unconscious patients
options.D: Testing superficial and deep tendon reflex strength

explanation: CT and MRI scans let doctors see cross-section pictures of what is happening inside the skull, like bleeding, swelling, or tumors. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h8)

question: What is the primary role of a community nurse during a home birth setting?

options.A: To replace traditional birth attendants without community consent
options.B: To bridge the gap between traditional practices and safe clinical care
options.C: To document births for statistical purposes only
options.D: To force every laboring mother to relocate to a tertiary hospital immediately

explanation: Community nurses work closely within local populations to provide safe, evidence-based care while respecting and understanding local birth choices. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h1)

question: A mother calls because her 2-day-old baby is super sleepy and won't feed at all. What should you suspect as a nurse?

options.A: A mild milk allergy needing a brand change
options.B: Normal newborn behavior that will fix itself
options.C: A serious hidden problem needing urgent medical review
options.D: Just normal tiredness from growing

explanation: Lethargy and refusing to feed are major warning signs in babies. It could point to infection, low blood sugar, or dehydration—always treat it as urgent! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h9)

question: How do barrier contraceptives help protect against cervical irritation?

options.A: They physically block infectious microorganisms from reaching the cervical mucosa.
options.B: They permanently seal the transformation zone to stop cellular changes.
options.C: They eliminate all normal bacteria living inside the reproductive tract.
options.D: They automatically increase natural estrogen levels in the vaginal canal.

explanation: Well done! Barrier methods like condoms act like a shield, stopping germs from making direct contact with the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h7)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when planning an IEC campaign?

options.A: Purchase expensive radio airtime for daily health broadcasts
options.B: Design colorful posters and print thousands of information leaflets
options.C: Organize a large community party with local musicians
options.D: Conduct a needs assessment to identify the actual problems of the community

explanation: Planning must always start with assessing the real needs and priorities of the community rather than guessing what they need. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why do certain medications need to be taken strictly on an empty stomach?

options.A: To ensure the liver enzymes are completely deactivated during digestion
options.B: To speed up the digestive process in the large intestine
options.C: To increase the overall acidity of the liver portal system
options.D: To prevent food from binding to the drug or delaying its absorption

explanation: Some foods love to mess with medications by chemically binding to them or slowing down how fast the stomach empties, which changes how much medicine actually gets into the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the lowest possible total score a patient can get on the Glasgow Coma Scale?
explanation: Since each of the three sections (Eyes, Verbal, Motor) has a minimum score of 1, the lowest total score possible is 3. (Even an unresponsive patient scores a 1 in each area!). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T7#GNS222_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is an outlier in a research dataset?

options.A: A missing patient file that was never collected
options.B: A category label used for nominal variables
options.C: The exact mathematical average of a frequency table
options.D: An extreme value that sits far away from other data points

explanation: Outliers are data entries that are unusually high or low compared to the vast majority of the observations in the dataset. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why do we strongly advise against using both hands to recap a needle?

options.A: It damages the sharpness of the needle tip
options.B: It makes the syringe difficult to read
options.C: It greatly increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.D: It takes too much time during an emergency

explanation: Spot on! Trying to guide a cap back on with two hands is a recipe for poking your own finger. Safety rules are written in blood—let's protect those fingers! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To sweep over the ovary and catch the released egg
options.B: To push sperm upward into the uterine cavity
options.C: To attach the ovary firmly to the pelvic wall
options.D: To secrete hormones that trigger monthly ovulation

explanation: The finger-like fimbriae use gentle sweeping movements to guide the newly released egg into the fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h3)

question: What does the round window do when the stapes pushes inward against the oval window?

options.C: It bulges outward to relieve fluid pressure in the cochlea
options.D: It seals shut to protect the delicate hair cells from damage

explanation: Since fluid cannot be squished into a smaller space, the round window acts as a pressure-relief valve, bulging outward every time the oval window pushes in. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main job of satellite cells in our skeletal muscles?

options.A: To repair and regenerate damaged muscle fibers
options.B: To remove lactic acid buildup after heavy exercise
options.C: To store calcium ions needed for sliding filaments
options.D: To produce the nerve signals that trigger contraction

explanation: Satellite cells are like little standby repair crew members. When muscle gets injured, they jump in to help fix and rebuild it! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why do kidney disease patients often need lower doses of certain antifungal medications?

options.A: Renal failure increases the absorption rate of topical creams

options.C: The kidneys are the main route for clearing the drug from the body
options.D: Damaged kidneys produce too much ergosterol, neutralizing the drug

question: Which home change is top priority when discharging a patient with serious balance and walking challenges?

options.A: Installing grab bars in the bathroom and removing loose rugs
options.B: Repainting all interior walls in bright, contrasting colors
options.C: Upgrading the home entertainment and television system
options.D: Replacing all hard flooring with thick, plush carpeting

explanation: Falls happen most often at home, especially in slick bathrooms and over sliding rugs. Securing these spots keeps our patients safe after they leave the hospital ward. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h7)

question: Why can extreme heat exposure during early pregnancy be risky for the developing baby?

options.A: It instantly changes the genetic blood type of the fetus
options.B: It triggers early puberty inside the womb
options.C: It causes the placenta to detach immediately on the first day
options.D: It can interfere with proper implantation and increase the risk of miscarriage

explanation: During early pregnancy, cells are dividing rapidly. High heat can disrupt this delicate process and put the pregnancy at risk. Every bit of knowledge gets you closer to exam success! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T15#GNS312_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which sign tells you a patient is struggling and working extra hard to breathe?

question: What is the main goal of medical asepsis in the ward?

options.C: To sterilize all medical instruments
options.D: To reduce the number of germs

question: During an EEG, the technician asks the client to breathe deeply and fast (hyperventilation). What happens in the body when you do this?

question: How many patient identifiers should a nurse check before giving a medication?

question: What is the main purpose of 'comfort feeding' in palliative care?

options.C: Strictly controlling blood sugar levels
options.D: Reversing severe malnutrition over time

question: What term is used to describe a dangerously low fasting blood sugar level?

question: What does the letter 'C' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey framework?

question: How do coenzymes help out enzymes?

question: What fluid do continuous glucose monitors sample to check a patient's sugar levels?

question: Besides providing support and protection, what mineral does compact bone primarily store?

question: At what point should you label a specimen container with the patient details?

question: Which of the following is an example of objective nutritional documentation?

question: Which structure acts like a lid to prevent food from entering the trachea during swallowing?

question: When caring for a patient with a cast, why should a nurse assess the whole patient and not just stare at the injury?

options.C: To measure the exact length of the bone healing underneath
options.D: To check if the patient is taking their pain medication on time

explanation: A bone injury doesn't happen in isolation! It can trigger widespread reactions throughout the body, so looking at the big picture helps you catch complications early. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h1)

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take when managing an active adverse drug reaction?

options.A: Discharging the patient home for proper rest

options.C: Starting broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately

question: Which medication do doctors commonly start early in pregnancy to help prevent pre-eclampsia in women with sickle cell disease?

options.A: High-dose hydroxyurea
options.B: Low-dose aspirin
options.C: Therapeutic penicillin
options.D: Intravenous iron sucrose

question: Which of these bones develops directly through intramembranous ossification?

options.C: Femur of the thigh
options.D: Flat bones of the skull

question: Why do joint sprains (injured ligaments) usually take a really long time to heal?

options.C: Fibrocartilage replaces all normal collagen
options.D: Ligaments have a poor blood supply

question: When a patient with peripheral arterial disease experiences "intermittent claudication," what does that feel like?

options.C: Sharp chest pain shooting down both arms while resting

question: Which of the following describes a key difference between screening tests and diagnostic tests in prenatal care?

options.A: Screening tests estimate risk, while diagnostic tests confirm a condition
options.B: Diagnostic tests are performed on every single pregnant woman
options.C: Screening tests are only done after birth
options.D: Screening tests use surgery, while diagnostic tests are painless

explanation: Screening tests only show the probability or risk of a disorder, whereas diagnostic tests provide a definitive diagnosis. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why do we prefer tube feeding (enteral nutrition) over drip feeding into a vein (parenteral nutrition) if the gut is working?

options.B: It is much cheaper and needs no equipment
options.C: It has zero risk of infection
options.D: It keeps the gut lining healthy and prevents it from wasting away

question: Which of these is one of the classic stages of grief identified by Elisabeth Kübler-Ross?

options.B: Bargaining
options.C: Resolution
options.D: Isolation

explanation: Spot on! Bargaining is a well-known stage where a person tries to negotiate a way out of the painful reality, like saying 'God, if you heal them, I will change my ways.' [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h3)

question: When did Nigeria introduce its first official National Drug Policy to fix chaotic drug distribution?

question: A patient says they can't follow their diabetic meal plan because fresh veggies are too expensive in their area. What is your best first nursing move?

options.A: Ignore the comment and repeat the original dietary brochure word for word
options.B: Advise the patient to stop eating vegetables entirely and take vitamin pills
options.C: Explore affordable alternatives like frozen or canned vegetables and consult social work
options.D: Tell the patient that buying fresh vegetables is mandatory for survival

explanation: Be a problem solver! Listen to their financial hurdles and help them find budget-friendly swaps so they can still eat healthy without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h7)

question: What does active listening primarily require from the nurse?

options.A: Focusing mostly on filling out the clinic register correctly
options.B: Writing down every single word the patient says in a notebook
options.C: Interrupting the patient quickly to save time during busy hours
options.D: Giving undivided attention and letting the patient finish speaking

question: What action should a nurse take immediately if a medication administration error occurs?

options.D: Report it to the doctor and nurse manager right away

question: A patient with lung cancer is still getting chemotherapy while also receiving care for severe pain and shortness of breath. What kind of approach is this?

options.B: Treating the side effects of chemotherapy exclusively with surgery
options.C: Abandoning curative treatment in favor of hospice
options.D: Stopping all medical interventions to allow natural death

question: Where should a nurse document an accidental medication mishap or patient fall?

options.A: Inside the personal diary of the ward manager
options.B: On the front cover of the patient's bed chart
options.C: In a public text message sent to local news stations
options.D: On a separate institutional incident report form

explanation: Incident reports are kept separate from the official medical record to track safety data and improve hospital systems. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)

question: Which of these devices is a great example of therapeutic equipment used to treat a patient?

options.B: Nebulizer
options.C: Thermometer
options.D: Stethoscope

explanation: Therapeutic equipment actively helps treat conditions and aids recovery. A nebulizer does this brilliantly by delivering medication straight to the airways! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: What happens when a patient lacks essential haematinics?

options.A: Red blood cell production is impaired
options.B: White blood cells multiply uncontrollably
options.C: Platelets aggregate too quickly in vessels

question: A young female patient has lower abdominal pain and cries out in severe pain when the nurse moves her cervix during a pelvic exam. What is the most likely condition?

options.B: Primary dysmenorrhea
options.C: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

question: Why can a poor shift handover easily lead to a malpractice claim?

options.A: It automatically causes patients to fall out of their hospital beds

options.C: It forces doctors to perform nursing duties they are not trained for
options.D: It breaks hospital labor laws regarding nursing shift lengths

question: When membranes rupture and the amniotic fluid is clear, what letter do you write on the partograph?

question: Why should a nurse gently press the inner corner of the eye (punctal occlusion) right after giving eye drops?

options.B: To clean away sticky discharge
options.C: To keep the medicine from getting into the rest of the body
options.D: To keep the pupil wide open

question: A community nurse wants to store the medical history of a husband, wife, and their children together in one file. Which stationery item should be used?

question: Why do medications absorb so slowly when given as an intradermal injection?

options.C: The needle gauge is too small to release much fluid
options.D: The outer layer of skin blocks fluid movement

question: In rehabilitation, what do we mean when we talk about setting SMART goals?

options.A: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
options.B: Safe, Medical, Active, Realistic, Team-oriented
options.C: Systematic, Managed, Assessed, Recorded, Tested

question: Why is continuous cardiac monitoring especially important for patients recovering from a heart attack?

question: Which of these is NOT one of the classic 'Six Ps' of acute limb ischemia?

options.C: Pain
options.D: Pulselessness

question: Why should a nurse adjust the weighing scale to zero before weighing every child?
